attention_subtype_map.causal_path: For FP8 KV cache, TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend clones local K and V only because set_kv_buffer scales them in place before _fwd_kernel consumes the originals. Enqueueing the local cache quantize/store after _fwd_kernel preserves same-stream ordering and removes both full-tensor clones without gathering KV or changing model/kernel geometry.

subtypes.source_semantics: extend/prefill; post-median-TTFT launches are dynamic-chunk prefill interleaved with decode
extend/prefill; post-median-TTFT launches are dynamic-chunk prefill interleaved with decode

attribution.attribution_rule: Every wall interval is assigned once. Concurrent GPU intervals use the longest active kernel; idle intervals use active CUDA synchronization/launch APIs, then scheduler_gap.

phases.split_rule: Non-overlapping median-TTFT proxy: prefill ends at the median first-token timestamp; the remainder is decode.

intervention.candidate_path_gate: candidate audit must contain phase=runtime_invocation, qk_head_dim=288, v_head_dim=256, sliding_window_size=1024, and removed_operations=[k.clone,v.clone]
intervention.source_justification: Pinned v0.5.13 TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend calls set_kv_buffer before extend_attention_fwd. With FP8 KV cache, set_kv_buffer descales K/V in place, so the backend protects the tensors with k.clone() and v.clone() before _fwd_kernel consumes them. For local sliding layers only, enqueueing the same cache commit after extend_attention_fwd preserves CUDA-stream dependence and exact attention inputs while eliminating two full BF16 tensor clones. It does not gather KV, alter heads/model geometry, substitute a backend, or tune KV splits/flags.
